verdict: Ball's sales rose 24% to $4.19B on higher aluminum prices and volumes, but a $475M non-cash charge for buying out its UK pension plan pushed it to a $94M GAAP loss; underlying comparable EPS rose 7% to $1.10.

kpis.label: Net sales
kpis.note: +24% vs a year ago, mostly aluminum price pass-through

kpis.label: Global shipments
kpis.note: More cans shipped in every region

segments.name: Beverage Packaging, North & Central America
segments.note: Drink cans for the U.S., Canada and Mexico — higher volumes and aluminum prices passed through to customers.

segments.name: Beverage Packaging, EMEA
segments.note: Cans across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, including the acquired Benepack business.

segments.name: Beverage Packaging, South America
segments.note: Cans in Brazil and neighbors — the fastest growth, on volume and price/mix.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Aluminum aerosol containers and other smaller businesses.

opex.name: Business consolidation & other activities
opex.note: Dominated by a $475M non-cash settlement charge for buying out the U.K. defined-benefit pension plan, plus facility-closure costs, partly offset by a favorable tariff ruling.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of can plants and equipment over their lives.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running and selling — a lean 3.4% of sales.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $75M, partly offset by $7M of interest income and $8M of equity income from affiliates (which Ball reports below its tax line).

takeaways.title: Sales jumped to $4.19B
takeaways.text: Most of the increase is aluminum: can prices carry a metal pass-through, so revenue inflates with the aluminum price. Underneath, shipments grew a healthy 4.7%.

takeaways.title: A pension buy-out charge
takeaways.text: Ball transferred its U.K. pension obligations to an insurer; accounting rules required recognizing a $475M non-cash settlement charge, swinging the quarter to a GAAP loss.

takeaways.title: Underlying EPS rose 7%
takeaways.text: Excluding the pension charge and similar items, comparable EPS was $1.10 and comparable operating earnings rose 2.5% to $451M.

oneTimers: The $475M pension settlement charge is non-cash: it recognizes previously deferred pension losses in one go as the U.K. plan is bought out. It does not change Ball's cash position or its ongoing pension costs (which fall).
footerNote: Equity income from affiliates ($8M), which Ball reports below its tax line, is included in the other-expense line so the flow reconciles to the reported net loss.
